stages.objective: Define the metadata contract and implement portable, rebuildable local persistence that loads note and folder metadata into workspace tree entries. Choose a storage format consistent with the repository’s local-first and Markdown constraints.
completion_criteria: Notes and folders can represent optional tags, emoji icon, favorite status, and created/updated timestamps in shared domain types.

Metadata storage can be reconstructed by reading its persisted representation and is not required for note content.

stages.title: Metadata lifecycle operations
stages.objective: Keep metadata consistent when notes and folders are created, edited, moved, renamed, or deleted, including updating timestamps where appropriate.
completion_criteria: Create and metadata-edit operations persist metadata for notes and folders through workspace services.
Note content updates advance the updated timestamp while preserving created time and other metadata.
Move, rename, and delete operations keep persisted metadata aligned with the affected workspace items.
Metadata writes follow the repository’s data-safety conventions and handle conflicting or failed writes without silently losing metadata.

stages.title: Metadata application state and UI
stages.objective: Wire metadata through desktop application state and expose controls and displays for note and folder metadata, without adding MCP support.
completion_criteria: Application state can read and update metadata using the shared workspace services.
The UI displays metadata for notes and folders and provides ways to edit tags and emoji icons and toggle favorite status.
Created and updated timestamps are visible in an appropriate note or folder UI surface.
Metadata changes refresh the relevant tree and editor views without requiring a workspace reopen.

history.summary: Implement local note and folder metadata through a shared data contract, workspace persistence and lifecycle operations, then expose it in application state and the UI. Keep MCP exposure deferred and preserve existing Markdown files without requiring migration.
